# Mohamed Bennamane — Full Profile

> Robotics & AI engineering student at NHSAST (National Higher School of Autonomous Systems Technologies), Sidi Abdellah, Algiers, Algeria.

## Personal Summary

I'm a second-year preparatory engineering student at NHSAST. I teach Analysis 2 through Epsilite, a volunteer tutoring program I co-manage. I've built web platforms used by hundreds of students, co-authored an Analysis II textbook with Dr. Zeglaoui (200+ pages), authored the solo 219-page Analysis I Companion Book, and competed in robotics.

Currently, I'm an active member of Team Delta, NHSAST's robotics team preparing for the AST Festival across 7 competition entries, from sumo robots to an all-terrain rover.

I'm also the AI Manager at IEEE NHSAST and the Event Manager at ASTCS. I organized events like Seed 2 and the AST Birthday celebration, and I'm part of planning the next Festival. I also created Unfalables, a philosophical debate competition where teams argue opposing positions under timed rounds.

Most of what I build comes from running into a problem and deciding to fix it: misleading info about NHSAST led to NHSAST-Info, students struggling with modules led to Epsilite, parents calling the teacher every 5 minutes during trips led to the Trips Tracker.

---

## Projects

### 01. NHSAST-Info — Web Platform (Arabic i18n)

**Problem:** When I got my bac in 2025 and started looking into NHSAST, I ran into misleading information everywhere. There was no centralized, honest resource about the school.

**What I built:**
- A guided tour walking prospective students through the school from scratch
- Specialization pages with introductions written by students in each field, covering career paths, market outlook, and honest advice
- Facility details (study room hours, library), official preparatory syllabus, club info with event photos and social links
- Epsilite section, FAQ page, and Students' Opinion page with both positives and negatives
- Ask Us page linking to a Telegram group with tagged NHSAST students ready to answer questions
- Full Arabic support with seamless RTL rendering so parents can read about what their kids will study

**Role:** Solo. Wrote all content, designed the interface, and built the site.
**Impact:** 1,500+ visitors during the specialty-choosing period. Multiple students confirmed the information and clarity was their main reason for picking the school.
**Tech:** Next.js, Tailwind CSS, i18n (EN/AR + RTL), Vercel
**Links:** https://nhsast-info.vercel.app

---

### 02. Epsilite — Academic Platform & LaTeX

**Problem:** NHSAST runs a 2-year general prep cycle followed by 3 years of specialization. Students struggle with the dense module load and there was no organized peer-to-peer academic support.

**What I built:**
- Co-founded a volunteer tutoring program where students create exercise sets, re-explain hard parts, produce summaries, cheat sheets, and exams at defined difficulty levels
- Taught Analysis 2 (calculus) alongside two other teachers, managed the first-year side
- Created exercise sets, exams, midterms, summaries, and cheat sheets in LaTeX
- Built markdown-to-LaTeX templates so other teachers could style their materials without learning LaTeX
- Built the Epsilite web platform: teachers are admins who publish resources, students browse everything, with per-document view tracking

**Role:** Co-founded and managed. Taught calculus. Built the entire platform and LaTeX template system.
**Impact:** Main resource during exam periods. 1,300+ visits during catch-up exams. 35+ students per study session. Planning expansion to other higher schools in Sidi Abdellah.
**Tech:** Next.js, Tailwind CSS, LaTeX, Vercel, Analytics
**Links:** https://epsilite.vercel.app

---

### 03. Analysis II Textbook — Co-Author

**Problem:** NHSAST prep students need rigorous, well-structured material for Analysis II. The existing professor's notes were dense and hard to study from independently.

**What I built:**
- Co-authored a full calculus textbook with Dr. Zeglaoui covering sequences, series, continuity, differentiability, and integration
- 200+ pages, 23+ revision rounds including mathematical audits, pedagogical reviews, and visual styling
- Written entirely in LaTeX with custom styling: flowcharts for proof strategies, cheat sheets per chapter, TikZ diagrams
- Used AI as a tool for LaTeX templates and formatting, not to write the math

**Role:** Co-author with Dr. Zeglaoui. Full LaTeX production, styling, and revision management.
**Impact:** Pending publication. Used by students during exam preparation.
**Tech:** LaTeX, TikZ, Pedagogical Design, Mathematical Auditing

---

### 04. Analysis I Companion Book — Sole Author

**Problem:** First semester Analysis is one of the steepest hurdles for new engineering students. Available materials treat analysis as detached formalism without showing how it governs autonomous systems.

**What I built:**
- 219-page companion textbook spanning the real number system, sequence convergence, functional continuity, differentiability, and asymptotic analysis
- Embedded real autonomous systems applications: ADC quantization, discrete proportional control errors, scalar Kalman filter variance updates, attitude angle estimation
- Three-tier progressive problem sets from foundational checks to advanced problems drawn from French CPGE Math Sup/Spé, Algerian competitions, and MIT OpenCourseWare
- Pedagogical tools: Proof Strategy Menu, Cross-Chapter Logical Traps with counterexamples, full mock exams with step-by-step corrections
- Full LaTeX/TikZ production with custom architectural layouts and vector cover art

**Role:** Sole author and typesetter.
**Impact:** Primary reference and exam prep companion for first-year NHSAST students.
**Tech:** LaTeX, TikZ, Pedagogical Design, CPGE & MIT OCW Curricula

---

### 05. POLYMAZE Robot — Robotics Competition

**Problem:** POLYMAZE is a maze-solver competition. I needed to design, build, and program a robot that autonomously navigates a maze.

**What I built:**
- 3D-printed chassis designed in SolidWorks with battery slide-in mounts and PCB seat
- Circuit with QTR line sensors and ESP32-WROOM controlling an H-bridge motor driver
- Maze-solving algorithm in C++
- ESP32 burned out 2 hours before deadline because I used solder as conductor instead of wires
- Rebuilt entire setup on a breadboard with L298N motor driver in the final minutes

**Role:** Solo. Chassis design, circuit wiring, code, and panicked breadboard rebuild.
**Impact:** Qualified with the breadboard robot. Made it to Phase 2. Finished 3rd in group.
**Tech:** ESP32, L298N Driver, QTR Sensors, C++, SolidWorks, 3D Printing

---

### 06. Team Delta — AST Festival (Competitive Robotics)

**What I'm building:**
- Part of Team Delta at NHSAST, building robots for 7 competition entries: Dog Robot, Sumo Robot, Rocket League, All-Terrain (6-wheel rocker-bogie), Maze Solver, Line Follower, and Innovation Project
- Working on CAD designs, mechanical fabrication, and embedded control
- Built the Team Delta showcase website for festival visitors and sponsors

**Role:** Team member. Building robots and developing the team website.
**Tech:** ESP32, SolidWorks, PCB Design, Embedded C, Next.js, Tailwind CSS

---

### 07. Expand Trips Tracker — Telemetry & Live Tracking

**Problem:** During school trips, parents repeatedly call the teacher to ask where the bus is.

**What I built:**
- Live bus tracking: teacher shares Telegram Live Location, webhook ingests GPS, parents see bus moving on a map
- Admin dashboard generates unique teacher passkey and parent link per trip
- Leaflet map with live/offline status, recenter button, Google Maps deep link for traffic/ETA
- Battery protection: polling pauses when phone is locked, hard-stops when trip completes
- Total cost: $0/month — Vercel free tier, Vercel KV, Telegram Bot API

**Role:** Solo. Everything from Telegram bot to parent-facing map.
**Tech:** Next.js, Leaflet.js, Telegram Bot API, Vercel KV
